relevance.rationale: *** WRONG JOIN ***. The seeded id points at a two-author 1994 quantum-dilogarithm entry. The document's own title page shows a FOUR-author paper on perturbative Chern-Simons theory with complex gauge group (arXiv:0903.2472v1, hep-th); none of its authors is the first author of the seeded entry, and the year differs. id set to null: no registered key matches (greps for '0903.2472' and for the third author's surname in references.ts are both empty). Judged on its own merits this is a CORE-relevance document rather than background. It constructs the all-loop perturbative invariants of complex Chern-Simons theory and the state-integral formalism on which the corpus's entire Q_beta / resurgence chapter rests: QOU/QBeta/StateIntegralRecursionLattice.lean, PhibSaddleA1Exact.lean, PhiBProdDivisor.lean, OneInstantonNormalization.lean and mass-theory/stokes-dt-bps-bridge.md all work with state integrals, and the corpus registers and cites three of this paper's descendants (garoufalidis-gu-marino2021, dimofte-garoufalidis, dimofte-gaiotto-gukov2013) while the foundational document itself is unregistered. That is a citation-hygiene gap, not merely an unused upload.

proposedActions.rationale: The foundational all-loop complex-Chern-Simons / state-integral paper underlying the corpus's Q_beta resurgence chapter has no ref() entry, while three of its descendants do. Register it from its own title page (arXiv:0903.2472).
Once registered, the state-integral definition used in QOU/QBeta should point at its actual origin rather than only at the later GGM/DGG papers.

entry.note: Source IS held: library/arxiv-0903.2472v1. The ledger recorded it as unavailable, so corpus-grep path 5 reported the repo does not have it — which sends an agent to re-derive a result it could have cited. Re-pointed from the measurement in scripts/cited-source-availability-audit.py.
